These two simple cases illustrate that the existence result (Theorem 3) holds for every
probability matrix κ, in particular reducible ones. The irreducibility condition on κ comes
into play to characterize the functions canceling the dissipation of entropy (Lemma 2),
which then proves crucial to establish uniqueness of the steady state and convergence
towards it.
